body.name: Worked three-policy closure test bed
body.construction: In \(\mathfrak E^\dagger\), compatibility is nonvacuous: for each of the six nonzero cells \((r,x)\), let \(t^{r,x}\) have \(N_r^{11}=4x\), \(N_r^{00}=4-4x\), \(N_s^{00}=4\) for \(s\ne r\), and every other response count zero. If \(N^\dagger\) places one cluster at each \(t^{r,x}\), then \(Q_{t^{r,x},r}(x)=1\) and \(N^\dagger\in\mathcal N(H^\dagger)\). Let \(\uparrow\) denote upward closure in the ordered-partition lattice and form \(\mathcal U_{12}=\uparrow\{\mathcal O:1\succ_{\mathcal O}2\}\), \(\mathcal U_{23}=\uparrow\{\mathcal O:2\succ_{\mathcal O}3\}\), and \(\mathcal U_{123}=\mathcal U_{12}\cap\mathcal U_{23}\). For any such intersection \(\mathcal U\) and an intersection-specific statistic \(T_{\mathcal U}\), the response-table oracle evaluates \[p_{\mathcal U}(H^\dagger)=\max_{\substack{N\in\mathcal N(H^\dagger)\colon\ \mathcal O(N)\in\mathcal U}}\sum_{h\in\mathcal H(N)}\mathsf P_N(h)\mathbf 1\!\left\{T_{\mathcal U}((\sum_t h_{trx})_{r,x})\ge T_{\mathcal U}(H^\dagger)\right\}.\] The construction handle is to choose the family \(T_{\mathcal U}\), apply closure to these lattice upper sets, and seek \(\widehat{\mathfrak O}^{\mathrm{cl}}_{\alpha}(H^\dagger)\subsetneq\widehat{\mathfrak O}_{\alpha}(H^\dagger)\) while retaining uniform coverage and consonance.
